title: SAF Air Defenses Intercept RSF Long-Range Drone Over White Nile State
detail: The Sudanese Armed Forces announced the interception of a long-range RSF drone over White Nile State on May 31, 2026, following a series of RSF aerial attacks on towns and vital facilities in the region. SAF air defense units engaged and shot down the incoming drone before it could strike its intended target. The interception demonstrates SAF's improving counter-drone capabilities in White Nile State, a critical rear-area logistics zone connecting Khartoum to southern Sudan. RSF has mounted repeated drone attacks on White Nile State throughout spring 2026 — including the Al-Jabalain Hospital strike (April 3, killing 10 including 7 medical staff), Rabak medical depot strike (April 3–4), SAF 18th Infantry Division HQ and Kenana airbase (April 29), Kenana fuel station (May 3), and Kosti fuel stations (May 5, killing 5). The May 31 interception is the first publicly confirmed SAF drone shoot-down over White Nile State since the escalation of RSF attacks in spring 2026. SAF has progressively deployed anti-drone systems to protect rear-area infrastructure as RSF extended its drone reach to 800+ km.

title: SAF Launches Drone Strikes on RSF Positions in North Kordofan Following White Nile Drone Interception
detail: The Sudanese Armed Forces launched drone strikes targeting RSF positions in North Kordofan State on May 31, 2026, following the SAF interception of an RSF drone over White Nile State and continuing the air interdiction campaign that has supported the SAF ground counteroffensive throughout May. North Kordofan remains the critical corridor linking RSF-held Darfur to central Sudan; SAF has been systematically degrading RSF logistics along this axis since the Kordofan counteroffensive began in earnest. May 2026 SAF ground gains include the Dibebad crossroads (May 22–23), Dilling siege break (May 19–20 for the third time), and Wadi al-Atrun trans-Saharan supply route capture (May 19). The drone campaign from May 27–31 maintains operational pressure on RSF North Kordofan elements following the Eid al-Adha period. SAF has not provided specific casualty figures; RSF has not publicly acknowledged losses in North Kordofan from this campaign period.
